**Max Emilian Verstappen** (Dutch pronunciation: [[ˈmɑks fɛrˈstɑpə(n)]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch")[racing driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_driver "Racing driver") who competes [under the Dutch flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_the_Netherlands "Formula One drivers from the Netherlands") in [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") for [Red Bull Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing"). Verstappen has won four [Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_World_Drivers'_Championship_titles "Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles"), which he won consecutively from [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship") to [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship "2024 Formula One World Championship") with Red Bull, and has won 74 [Grands Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_Grands_Prix "Formula One Grands Prix") across 12 seasons.
Born in [Hasselt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasselt "Hasselt") and raised in [Maaseik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maaseik "Maaseik"), Verstappen is the son of Dutch former Formula One driver [Jos Verstappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Verstappen "Jos Verstappen") and Belgian former [kart racer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racer "Kart racer") [Sophie Kumpen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Kumpen "Sophie Kumpen"). After a successful karting career—culminating in his [record-breaking 2013 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#2013:_Record-breaking_season)—Verstappen graduated to [junior formulae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_formulae "Junior formulae"). Progressing directly to [FIA European Formula 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Formula_3_European_Championship "FIA Formula 3 European Championship"), Verstappen broke several records on his way to third in the championship in [his rookie season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIA_Formula_3_European_Championship "2014 FIA Formula 3 European Championship") with [Van Amersfoort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Amersfoort "Van Amersfoort").[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-3) Aged 17, Verstappen signed for [Toro Rosso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toro_Rosso "Toro Rosso") in [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Formula_One_World_Championship "2015 Formula One World Championship") as part of the [Red Bull Junior Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Junior_Team "Red Bull Junior Team"), becoming the [youngest driver in Formula One history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Youngest_drivers_to_start_a_race "List of Formula One driver records") at the [Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Australian_Grand_Prix "2015 Australian Grand Prix"). Following several points finishes in his debut season, Verstappen retained his seat for [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Formula_One_World_Championship "2016 Formula One World Championship") before being promoted to parent team [Red Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing") to partner [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") after four rounds. On debut for Red Bull, aged 18, Verstappen won the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2016 Spanish Grand Prix"), becoming the [youngest-ever driver to win a Formula One Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Youngest_winners "List of Formula One driver records"). Verstappen achieved multiple race wins in his [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Formula_One_World_Championship "2017 Formula One World Championship") and [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Formula_One_World_Championship "2018 Formula One World Championship") campaigns, before finishing third in both the [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Formula_One_World_Championship "2019 Formula One World Championship") and [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Formula_One_World_Championship "2020 Formula One World Championship") World Drivers' Championships [under Honda power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One").
Verstappen won his maiden title in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship") after overtaking [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") on the final lap of the [last race of the season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"), becoming the [first World Drivers' Champion from the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_the_Netherlands "Formula One drivers from the Netherlands"). Verstappen won the next two championships in [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Formula_One_World_Championship "2022 Formula One World Championship") and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship"), overturning the largest points deficit in Formula One history in the former and breaking numerous records across both seasons.[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-4) He secured his fourth consecutive title in [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship "2024 Formula One World Championship") after winning nine Grands Prix, including a widely acclaimed wet-weather performance in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2024 São Paulo Grand Prix"), to become the first driver to win the championship driving for a third-placed constructor in [41 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Formula_One_World_Championship "1983 Formula One World Championship"). He finished runner-up by two points in a three-way title battle with [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris") and [Oscar Piastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Piastri "Oscar Piastri") in [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Formula_One_World_Championship "2025 Formula One World Championship").
As of the [2026 São Paulo Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2026 São Paulo Grand Prix"), Verstappen has achieved 74 race wins, 50 pole positions, 38 fastest laps, and 139 podiums in Formula One. In addition to being the youngest Grand Prix winner, he holds several [Formula One records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records "List of Formula One driver records"), including the [most wins in a season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_wins_in_a_season "List of Formula One driver records") (19), the [most podium finishes in a season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_podium_finishes_in_a_season "List of Formula One driver records") (21), the [most consecutive wins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_consecutive_wins "List of Formula One driver records") (10), and the [most consecutive pole positions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_consecutive_pole_positions "List of Formula One driver records") (8, shared with [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna")). Verstappen is contracted to remain at Red Bull until at least the end of the 2030 season. Outside of Formula One, Verstappen runs the [Verstappen Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#Verstappen_Racing) team, has competed in [sports car racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_car_racing "Sports car racing") events, and has also competed professionally in [sim racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim_racing "Sim racing") since 2015, winning several marquee _[iRacing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IRacing "IRacing")_ events. Verstappen was listed in the 2024 issue of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time \(magazine\)")_ as one of the [100 most influential people globally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_100 "Time 100"), and was appointed an [Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_Orange-Nassau "Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau") in 2022.
## Early life
Max Emilian Verstappen was born on 30 September 1997 in [Hasselt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasselt "Hasselt"), Belgium, to [Jos Verstappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Verstappen "Jos Verstappen") and [Sophie Kumpen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophie_Kumpen "Sophie Kumpen").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-5) Verstappen's parents separated when he was young, after which he lived with his father. His younger sister, Victoria, lived with their mother.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-6) Verstappen has three younger half-siblings from his father: a sister from Jos's second marriage and a brother and sister from Jos's current marriage.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-:2-7)
His family has a long association with motor sports: his father is a Dutch former Formula One driver, his Belgian mother competed in [karting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-racing_family2-8)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-nationality2-9) and his first cousin once removed, [Anthony Kumpen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Kumpen "Anthony Kumpen"), competed in endurance racing and is a two-time [NASCAR Whelen Euro Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASCAR_Whelen_Euro_Series "NASCAR Whelen Euro Series") champion currently serving as the team manager for [PK Carsport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PK_Carsport "PK Carsport") in Euro Series.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-racing_family2-8) Verstappen initially attended a secondary school in [Maaseik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maaseik "Maaseik"), before moving into [private tutoring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_tutor "Private tutor"); he admitted that he used to [leave class early](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truancy "Truancy") to attend races across Europe with his father.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-10)
## Junior racing career
### Karting (2005–2013)
#### 2005–2009: Dominance in national championships
Verstappen started racing in karts at the age of four and competing in championships at the age of seven. In 2005 he competed in the Mini Junior championship of his home province of [Limburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limburg_\(Belgium\) "Limburg \(Belgium\)"), Belgium,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-11) and won the [VAS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders") Championship in the same category. In 2006, he repeated his success. In 2007, Verstappen graduated to the [Rotax Max](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotax_Max "Rotax Max") Mini Max class and won the Rotax Max Challenge Belgium[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-12) and the Dutch Championship[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-13) in that category. In 2008, racing in a [CRG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CRG_\(kart_manufacturer\) "CRG \(kart manufacturer\)") kart entered by his father, Verstappen won the Belgian Cadet Championship,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-14) the Rotax Max Challenge Belgium,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-15) and the Benelux Karting Series in Mini Max class.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-16) In 2009, Verstappen joined Pex Racing, a CRG customer team. That year, he defended his titles in the Mini Max championships[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-17)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-18) and won the Belgian KF5 Championship.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-19)
#### 2010–2012: Entering the international karting scene
Verstappen was signed by CRG to race in their factory team and stepped up to international karting in 2010. At the [KF3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF3 "KF3") [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Karting_World_Championship "FIA Karting World Championship"), Verstappen finished second to the more experienced [Alexander Albon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Albon "Alexander Albon") (who eventually became his Formula One teammate at Red Bull Racing)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-20) but beat him at the [WSK Euro Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_WSK_Euro_Series "2010 WSK Euro Series")[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-21) and also won the WSK World Series, beating [Robert Vișoiu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Vi%C8%99oiu "Robert Vișoiu").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-22) He finished fifth in the [European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA_Karting_European_Championship "CIK-FIA Karting European Championship") and won the WSK Nations Cup[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-23) as well as the final of the Bridgestone Cup where during a 28 laps' race in the rain he beat [Dennis Olsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Olsen_\(racing_driver\) "Dennis Olsen \(racing driver\)") by over 11 seconds.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-24) In 2011, Verstappen won the [WSK Euro Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_WSK_Euro_Series "2011 WSK Euro Series") ahead of [Esteban Ocon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esteban_Ocon "Esteban Ocon") in a [Parilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_American_Motor_Engineering "Italian American Motor in the [World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Karting_World_Championship "FIA Karting World Championship") after an electrical failure while he and [Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc") were catching the drivers in front for the win.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-26)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-27)
In the following year, Verstappen joined the Intrepid Driver Program to race in the [KF2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2") and [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2") classes. He won the [WSK Master Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSK_Super_Master_Series "WSK Super Master Series") in the KF2 class, beating the CRG driver Felice Tiene.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-28) Verstappen won the South Garda Winter Cup in the KF2 class, beating [Dennis Olsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Olsen_\(racing_driver\) "Dennis Olsen \(racing driver\)") and [Antonio Fuoco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Fuoco "Antonio Fuoco").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-29)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-30) He finished sixth in the [WSK Euro Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSK_Euro_Series "WSK Euro Series").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-31) He was the youngest driver taking part in the World Championship in [KF1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF1 "KF1") class and finished eighth.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-32) In July 2012, it was announced that Verstappen would leave Intrepid. After a short stint with CRG-built [Zanardi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Zanardi "Alex Zanardi") karts, Verstappen returned to the factory CRG team.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-33) He finished second at the World Cup in the KF2 class[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-34) and competed at the SKUSA SuperNationals in the KZ2 class in a CRG, finishing 21st.
#### 2013: Record-breaking season
In 2013, Verstappen completed a record-breaking season in karting, having progressed to the senior [KF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2") and [KZ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ_\(karting\) "KZ \(karting\)") categories. Aged 15, he won three [CIK-FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIK-FIA "CIK-FIA") championships in a single season: two [European Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_European_Championship "Karting European Championship") and a [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship "Karting World Championship"); an unprecedented feat in the history of the discipline.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-35) He became the first driver since his father [Jos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Verstappen "Jos Verstappen") to win two European Championships in the same season, and the first to do so in both primary classes. By winning the 2013 [KZ World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship#Gearbox_class_\(1983%E2%80%932000,_2013%E2%80%93present\) "Karting World Championship") at [Varennes-sur-Allier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Varennes-sur-Allier "Varennes-sur-Allier"), beating [Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc") to the title, Verstappen became the youngest-ever driver to win the gearbox World Championship.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-37)
Further adding to his accolades in 2013, Verstappen also finished third at the [KF World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karting_World_Championship#FIA_Karting_World_champions_\(direct_drive_&_primary_category\) "Karting World Championship") after being disqualified for a move on [Nicklas Nielsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicklas_Nielsen "Nicklas Nielsen") in the final race, having won the opening round and pre-final.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-38) This was the only championship he failed to win in 2013 whilst completing all rounds. Verstappen won the South Garda Winter Cup in [KF2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KF2 "KF2"),[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-39) as well as the [WSK Euro Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSK_Euro_Series "WSK Euro Series") and the [WSK Super Master Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WSK_Super_Master_Series "WSK Super Master Series") in [KZ1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ1_\(karting\) "KZ1 \(karting\)") and [KZ2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KZ2 "KZ2"), respectively.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-40)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-41)
### Lower formulae (2014)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/2014_F3_HockenheimringII_Max_Verstappen_by_2eight_DSC6547.jpg/250px-2014_F3_HockenheimringII_Max_Verstappen_by_2eight_DSC6547.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2014_F3_HockenheimringII_Max_Verstappen_by_2eight_DSC6547.jpg)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/2014_F3_HockenheimringII_Max_Verstappen_by_2eight_DSC7625_%28cropped_less%29.jpg/120px-2014_F3_HockenheimringII_Max_Verstappen_by_2eight_DSC7625_%28cropped_less%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2014_F3_HockenheimringII_Max_Verstappen_by_2eight_DSC7625_\(cropped_less\).jpg)
Verstappen competed in the [FIA Formula 3 European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Formula_3_European_Championship "FIA Formula 3 European Championship") in [2014](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIA_Formula_3_European_Championship "2014 FIA Formula 3 European Championship"), after joining the [Red Bull Junior Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Junior_Team "Red Bull Junior Team").
Verstappen first experienced [formula racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_racing "Formula racing") at [Pembrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pembrey_Circuit "Pembrey Circuit") in August 2013 with [Manor MP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MP_Motorsport "MP Motorsport"); he drove 160 laps across two days in a [Barazi-Epsilon FR2.0–10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barazi-Epsilon#Barazi-Epsilon_FR2.0-10 "Barazi-Epsilon").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-42)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-43) He tested for several other [Formula Renault 2.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_Renault_2.0 "Formula Renault 2.0") teams that year.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-44) In December 2013, Verstappen tested a [Dallara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallara "Dallara") F311 [Formula Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_Three "Formula Three") car run by [Motopark Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motopark_Academy "Motopark Academy").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-45) An additional Formula Renault test followed in December at [Circuito de Jerez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_de_Jerez "Circuito de Jerez"). Driving for [Josef Kaufmann Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_Kaufmann_Racing "Josef Kaufmann Racing"), Verstappen went faster than Formula Renault regulars like [Steijn Schothorst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steijn_Schothorst "Steijn Schothorst") and [Matt Parry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Parry "Matt Parry").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-46) At the [Circuit Ricardo Tormo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_Ricardo_Tormo "Circuit Ricardo Tormo") near [Valencia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valencia "Valencia"), Verstappen set a faster lap time than the more experienced driver [Eddie Cheever III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Cheever_III "Eddie Cheever III").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-47)
#### 2014: Florida Winter Series and Formula Three
On 16 January 2014, it was announced Verstappen would make his [junior formulae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior_formulae "Junior formulae") debut in the non-championship [Florida Winter Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Winter_Series "Florida Winter Series").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-48) On 5 February, at the second race weekend, Verstappen won the race at [Palm Beach International Raceway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach_International_Raceway "Palm Beach International Raceway") after he started from pole.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-49) A few weeks later, Verstappen won his second race of the series at [Homestead–Miami Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead%E2%80%93Miami_Speedway "Homestead–Miami Speedway") after beating [Nicholas Latifi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Latifi "Nicholas Latifi") by 0.004 seconds.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-50)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-51)
Following his single-seater debut in the inaugural Florida Winter Series, Verstappen drove in the [2014 FIA Formula 3 European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIA_Formula_3_European_Championship "2014 FIA Formula 3 European Championship") for [Van Amersfoort Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Amersfoort_Racing "Van Amersfoort Racing").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-52) Aged sixteen, Verstappen achieved ten victories in total—including a record six consecutive wins at [Spa-Francorchamps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spa-Francorchamps "Spa-Francorchamps") and the [Norisring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norisring "Norisring")—along with eight retirements and one missed start, becoming the youngest race winner and polesitter in [Formula Three](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_Three "Formula Three") history at the [Hockenheimring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hockenheimring "Hockenheimring"); he placed third in the overall standings, with the most wins.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-53)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-54)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-55)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-56)
## Formula One career
During the first practice session at the [2014 Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2014 Japanese Grand Prix"), Verstappen replaced [Jean-Éric Vergne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-%C3%89ric_Vergne "Jean-Éric Vergne") as part of his preparation for a full-time seat at [Toro Rosso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Toro_Rosso "Scuderia Toro Rosso") in the [2015](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Formula_One_World_Championship "2015 Formula One World Championship") season.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-57) Aged 17 years and three days, Verstappen was the youngest person in history to participate in a Formula One race weekend.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-58) In August 2014, Verstappen joined the [Red Bull Junior Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Junior_Team "Red Bull Junior Team") after testing a Formula Renault 3.5 car. He also considered an offer from [Mercedes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") to join their [driver development programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes_Junior_Team "Mercedes Junior Team").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-59)
### Toro Rosso (2015–2016)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/db/Max_Verstappen_2015_Malaysia_Q2.jpg/250px-Max_Verstappen_2015_Malaysia_Q2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Verstappen_2015_Malaysia_Q2.jpg)Verstappen (pictured at the [2015 Malaysian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2015 Malaysian Grand Prix")) became the youngest driver in Formula One history at the [Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Australian_Grand_Prix "2015 Australian Grand Prix"), aged 17.
Verstappen then became the [youngest driver to start a World Championship race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Youngest_drivers_to_start_a_race "List of Formula One driver records") through joining Toro Rosso's race drivers' line-up with [Carlos Sainz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sainz_Jr. "Carlos Sainz Jr.") as his teammate, in his Grand Prix debut as a full-time driver at the [2015 Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Australian_Grand_Prix "2015 Australian Grand Prix") at the age of 17 years, 166 days—breaking [Jaime Alguersuari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaime_Alguersuari "Jaime Alguersuari")'s existing record by almost two years.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-60) In this first race, Verstappen ran in points-scoring positions until he was forced to retire due to an engine failure.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-61) However, at the subsequent race in [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2015 Malaysian Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified sixth and finished the race in seventh place, scoring his first Formula One points aged 17 years, 180 days, breaking the record of the then-[youngest driver to score World Championship points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Youngest_drivers_to_score_points "List of Formula One driver records").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-62)
At the [2015 Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2015 Monaco Grand Prix"), Verstappen was involved in a high-speed collision with [Romain Grosjean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romain_Grosjean "Romain Grosjean"), after clipping the back of Grosjean's [Lotus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotus_F1 "Lotus F1") on the approach to the tight first corner, Sainte Devote, and crashed into the barriers at high speed.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-63)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-64) Verstappen was given a five-place grid penalty for causing the accident, and was branded "dangerous" by [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering") driver [Felipe Massa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Massa "Felipe Massa").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-65) Verstappen continued to regularly finish in the points as well as achieving his best finish of the 2015 season in [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2015 Hungarian Grand Prix") by finishing fourth,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-66) and equalled this result at the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_United_States_Grand_Prix "2015 United States Grand Prix").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-67) At the end of the season, Verstappen received three awards at the [FIA Prize Giving Ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Prize_Giving_Ceremony "FIA Prize Giving Ceremony"), for "Rookie of the Year", "Personality of the Year" and "Action of the Year", for his overtake on [Felipe Nasr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Nasr "Felipe Nasr") on the outside of the Blanchimont corner at the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2015 Belgian Grand Prix").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-68)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-69)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Verstappen_Bahrain_2016.jpg/250px-Verstappen_Bahrain_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Verstappen_Bahrain_2016.jpg)Verstappen at the [2016 Bahrain Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2016 Bahrain Grand Prix")
Verstappen began the 2016 season at Toro Rosso, again alongside Sainz.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-70) Verstappen qualified fifth for the opening race of the season in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Australian_Grand_Prix "2016 Australian Grand Prix"), but during the race made several radio calls to his team due to frustration at being behind Sainz on track before Verstappen's Toro Rosso came into contact with his teammate's car whilst attempting to pass him with three laps to go, and he eventually finished tenth.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-71) Verstappen enjoyed a more successful weekend at the following race in [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2016 Bahrain Grand Prix"), finishing sixth to score Toro Rosso's first-ever points at the Sakhir circuit.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-72)
### Red Bull (2016–present)
#### 2016: Youngest Grand Prix winner
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/Verstappen_Spain_2016.jpg/250px-Verstappen_Spain_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Verstappen_Spain_2016.jpg)Verstappen celebrating victory at the [2016 Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2016 Spanish Grand Prix"), in his first race for the Red Bull Racing team
On 5 May 2016, following the [Russian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Russian_Grand_Prix "2016 Russian Grand Prix"), Red Bull Racing announced that Verstappen would be replacing Daniil Kvyat from the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2016 Spanish Grand Prix") onwards, with Kvyat returning to Toro Rosso.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-73) According to Red Bull Team Principal [Christian Horner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_Horner "Christian Horner"), "Max has proven to be an outstanding young talent. His performance at Toro Rosso has been impressive so far and we are pleased to give him the opportunity to drive for Red Bull Racing."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-RBR_Swap-74) After qualifying fourth for the Spanish Grand Prix,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Verstappen_4th_in_Qualifying-75) Verstappen rose to second behind teammate [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") on the opening lap after Mercedes teammates [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") and [Nico Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Rosberg "Nico Rosberg") crashed out of the race.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-76) Verstappen took the race lead as he was placed on a two-stop rather than the same three-stop strategy as Ricciardo, and he held off [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari")'s [Kimi Räikkönen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_R%C3%A4ikk%C3%B6nen "Kimi Räikkönen") in the later stages of the race to take his first Formula One victory.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-77)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-78) By doing so he displaced [Sebastian Vettel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel") as the youngest driver ever to win a Formula One Grand Prix at the age of 18 years and 228 days.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-:0-79) In his first eight races with Red Bull, he achieved six top-five finishes, including four podiums.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Standings-80)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/Podium_2016_Malaysia.jpg/250px-Podium_2016_Malaysia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Podium_2016_Malaysia.jpg)Verstappen on the podium with [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") and [Nico Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nico_Rosberg "Nico Rosberg") at the [2016 Malaysian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2016 Malaysian Grand Prix")
During the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2016 Belgian Grand Prix"), Verstappen collided with Räikkönen at the first corner, pushed Vettel, Räikkönen and Pérez wide at _Les Combes_ , and aggressively blocked Räikkönen on the Kemmel straight.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-81) Verstappen was criticised for his driving, with Räikkönen saying that he was "going to cause a huge accident sooner or later". Christian Horner noted that the driving was "on the edge", and that Verstappen will "look at it and learn for future races".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-82) In September, Formula One director [Charlie Whiting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Whiting "Charlie Whiting") called in Verstappen for a discussion, and later gave him a 'gentle warning' due to his aggressive driving.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-83) In October, drivers' concerns about Verstappen's defensive tactics led the FIA to disallow moving under braking.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-84)
At the [2016 Brazilian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Brazilian_Grand_Prix "2016 Brazilian Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified fourth.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-85) In a rain affected race, he almost hit the barrier after he slid on the main straight due to a loss of traction, causing [oversteer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oversteer "Oversteer").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-86) After an additional tyre change from intermediates back to rain tyres, he ran in 16th place with just 15 laps remaining. Verstappen then made several overtakes in quick succession during the closing laps to eventually finish on the podium in third place.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-87) He received considerable praise for his performance: rival team Mercedes' team principal, [Toto Wolff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toto_Wolff "Toto Wolff"), labelled it "The Verstappen Show", and described Verstappen's drive as "physics..being redefined".[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-88)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-89)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-90) However, Verstappen came under criticism from four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel, who stated that Verstappen had pushed him off the track at the Junção corner late in the race. The race stewards did not share Vettel's view and decided that no reprimand was warranted.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-91)
#### 2017–2018: Reliability issues and rise to prominence
[![Verstappen overtaking Lewis Hamilton for the lead of the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Max_Verstappen_overtaking_Lewis_Hamilton_2017_Malaysia_2.jpg/250px-Max_Verstappen_overtaking_Lewis_Hamilton_2017_Malaysia_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Verstappen_overtaking_Lewis_Hamilton_2017_Malaysia_2.jpg)Verstappen took his second career victory at the [Malaysian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2017 Malaysian Grand Prix") in [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Formula_One_World_Championship "2017 Formula One World Championship").
During the first 14 races of the 2017 season, Verstappen suffered seven retirements, four due to mechanical issues,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-92) and three due to first lap collisions in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2017 Spanish Grand Prix"), [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2017 Austrian Grand Prix") and [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2017 Singapore Grand Prix").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-93) Of the races he finished, however, he claimed a third place in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2017 Chinese Grand Prix"), and in another five races he finished fourth or fifth.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Standings-80) From the [Malaysian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2017 Malaysian Grand Prix") onward, Verstappen enjoyed a surge of success. He won his second Formula One race at the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix, a day after his 20th birthday, passing then three-time champion Lewis Hamilton for the lead in the early stages of the race.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-94) He finished second in the following [race in Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2017 Japanese Grand Prix").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-95) He then finished third at the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_United_States_Grand_Prix "2017 United States Grand Prix") Grand Prix, but was classified fourth after his final lap overtake on Kimi Räikkönen was deemed illegal.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-96) He won his third Formula One race at the [Mexican Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Mexican_Grand_Prix "2017 Mexican Grand Prix"), after passing [Sebastian Vettel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel") on the opening lap.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-97)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/2018_Spanish_Grand_Prix_Verstappen_%285%29.jpg/250px-2018_Spanish_Grand_Prix_Verstappen_%285%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2018_Spanish_Grand_Prix_Verstappen_\(5\).jpg)Verstappen at the [2018 Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2018 Spanish Grand Prix")
In the first six races of the [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Formula_One_World_Championship "2018 Formula One World Championship") season, Verstappen had been involved in at least one incident in each race. In [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Australian_Grand_Prix "2018 Australian Grand Prix"), he qualified fourth but fell behind [Kevin Magnussen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Magnussen "Kevin Magnussen") at the start.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-98) In his attempts to retake the position he ran wide multiple times and damaged his car, with a spin causing him to fall further down the order. He recovered to eventually finish the race in sixth place.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-99) At the next race in [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2018 Bahrain Grand Prix"), he crashed during qualifying and started in 15th place.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-100) He had a productive first lap after which he found himself in the points while challenging Lewis Hamilton. He attempted an overtake on the reigning World Champion at the start of lap two, but collided with the Mercedes driver and suffered a puncture that ultimately led to suspension damage, forcing him out of the race.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-101)
At the next race in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2018 Chinese Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified fifth and had moved up to third at the end of the first lap.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-102) Both Red Bull drivers pitted for fresh tyres during a safety car which left them with a tyre advantage over the front-runners ahead. In an overtake attempt on [Sebastian Vettel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel") for third place, Verstappen collided with the championship leader, causing him to fall to eighth and receive a 10-second penalty.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-103) He recovered to fourth place, with his penalty causing him to be classified fifth. Teammate Ricciardo went on to win the race.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-104) In [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2018 Azerbaijan Grand Prix"), Verstappen was embroiled in a race-long battle with Ricciardo for fourth place. After numerous position changes between the two teammates during the race, Ricciardo ran into the back of Verstappen during an overtake attempt from which the Dutchman aggressively defended, causing the retirement of both cars.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-105) Both drivers were blamed by the team and reprimanded by the stewards.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-106) Verstappen bounced back in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2018 Spanish Grand Prix") with his first podium of the season by finishing third behind the Mercedes drivers, holding off [Sebastian Vettel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel"). However, the race was also not without incident as he had run into the back of [Lance Stroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Stroll "Lance Stroll") during the virtual safety car period, causing minor front wing damage.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-107)
In [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2018 Monaco Grand Prix"), Verstappen made another error and crashed near the end of the third free practice session in an incident which closely resembled a crash he had at the same spot [two years earlier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Monaco_Grand_Prix#Qualifying "2016 Monaco Grand Prix").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-108) His team could not repair his car in time for qualifying and Verstappen had to start the race from the back of the grid.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-:1-109) Verstappen did not compete and did not set a lap time in qualifying, therefore teammate Ricciardo pressed home Red Bull's advantage at the track by taking [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pole_position "Pole position") and the race win. Verstappen managed to salvage two points by finishing ninth place, overtaking six cars on track.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-110) Team principal Christian Horner commented on Verstappen's start of the season, saying he "needed to stop making these mistakes" and that he could "learn from his teammate", while [Helmut Marko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Marko "Helmut Marko"), head of driver development at Red Bull, said that Verstappen was "too impatient".[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-:1-109) Verstappen now lay in sixth place in the championship with 35 points, only three points ahead of [Fernando Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso") in the McLaren, and 37 points behind his teammate in third, who had taken two wins in the first six races.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-111)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-112)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0b/2018_Austrian_Grand_Prix_podium_%2829388813658%29.jpg/250px-2018_Austrian_Grand_Prix_podium_%2829388813658%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2018_Austrian_Grand_Prix_podium_\(29388813658\).jpg)Verstappen celebrating on the podium with [Kimi Räikkönen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_R%C3%A4ikk%C3%B6nen "Kimi Räikkönen") and [Sebastian Vettel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebastian_Vettel "Sebastian Vettel") after winning the [2018 Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2018 Austrian Grand Prix")
In [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Canadian_Grand_Prix "2018 Canadian Grand Prix"), Verstappen topped all three practice sessions and qualified third, two-tenths off Sebastian Vettel in pole position.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-113) He eventually finished third and set the fastest lap of the race.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-114) The following race in [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_French_Grand_Prix "2018 French Grand Prix") brought him second place.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-115) In [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2018 Austrian Grand Prix")—Red Bull's home track, he started fourth on the grid, passed Kimi Räikkönen before taking advantage of retirement from [Valtteri Bottas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valtteri_Bottas "Valtteri Bottas") and a botched pit-stop strategy by Lewis Hamilton, who later had to retire from fourth place, to claim the fourth race victory of his career.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-116) In [Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_British_Grand_Prix "2018 British Grand Prix"), Verstappen was plagued by issues, finishing the first practice session early due to a gearbox problem and crashing in the second practice session before retiring from the race due to a brake problem.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-117) He would then finish fourth in [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_German_Grand_Prix "2018 German Grand Prix") after strategy errors let a recovering Hamilton get past him as he went on to win the race.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-118) Verstappen ended the first half of the season with a retirement in [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2018 Hungarian Grand Prix") and was narrowly behind his teammate in the championship due to his own recent resurgence and Ricciardo's unreliability.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-119)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-120)
Verstappen enjoyed a very strong second half of the season, achieving podium finishes in [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2018 Belgian Grand Prix"), [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2018 Singapore Grand Prix"), [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2018 Japanese Grand Prix") and the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_United_States_Grand_Prix "2018 United States Grand Prix"), the latter of which he achieved second place having started from 18th on the grid due to a suspension failure in qualifying.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-121) Following the qualifying session at the [Mexican Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Mexican_Grand_Prix "2018 Mexican Grand Prix"), Verstappen revealed that a mechanical problem with his Red Bull under braking cost him any chance of becoming the youngest-ever Formula One pole-sitter. As a result, Ricciardo beat Verstappen to pole position by just 0.026 seconds.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-122)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-123) Verstappen had a better start than Ricciardo and took the lead of the race into the first corner, overtaking the fast-starting Mercedes of Lewis Hamilton. Verstappen earned his fifth career win in Mexico.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-124)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-125) He was poised to win the [2018 Brazilian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Brazilian_Grand_Prix "2018 Brazilian Grand Prix"), having overtaken Räikkönen, Vettel, Bottas, and Hamilton. However, he collided with [Force India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Force_India "Force India") driver [Esteban Ocon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esteban_Ocon "Esteban Ocon") who was trying to unlap himself on faster tyres.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-126) Ocon received a 10-second stop-and-go penalty for the incident. After the collision with Ocon, Verstappen finished in second place behind Hamilton. During an argument with Ocon after the race, Verstappen pushed the Force India driver, for which he was given two days of "public service" as a penalty by the FIA.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-127) He then finished his season with another podium as he finished third in Abu Dhabi.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-128) Verstappen ended the season in fourth place in the championship with 249 points, claiming two wins, eleven podium finishes, and two fastest laps.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-129)
#### 2019–2020: Dominating teammates
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Max_Verstappen_during_Hungarian_Formula_1_GP.jpg/250px-Max_Verstappen_during_Hungarian_Formula_1_GP.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Verstappen_during_Hungarian_Formula_1_GP.jpg)Verstappen at the [2019 Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2019 Hungarian Grand Prix"), where he started on pole position for the first time in his career
In [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Formula_One_World_Championship "2019 Formula One World Championship"), Red Bull switched from Renault to [Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One") power units.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-130) After Ricciardo moved to the [Renault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renault_in_Formula_One "Renault in Formula One") team for 2019, Verstappen was joined at Red Bull by [Pierre Gasly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Gasly "Pierre Gasly").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-131) Verstappen qualified in fourth and finished third in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Australian_Grand_Prix "2019 Australian Grand Prix"), the first podium finish for a [Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One")-powered driver since the [2008 British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_British_Grand_Prix "2008 British Grand Prix").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-132) Verstappen was on course for a second third-place finish in [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2019 Bahrain Grand Prix") before a late safety car prevented him from overtaking Charles Leclerc's ailing Ferrari, keeping him in fourth place.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-133) Two more fourth-place finishes followed in [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2019 Chinese Grand Prix") and [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2019 Azerbaijan Grand Prix"), and a podium in [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2019 Spanish Grand Prix") in third place.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-134)[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-135)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-136) In [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2019 Monaco Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified in third place. He was released into the path of Valtteri Bottas during the drivers' pit stops, gaining second place but receiving a 5-second penalty as a result. Verstappen crossed the line in second place but was demoted to fourth by the penalty.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-137)
In [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Canadian_Grand_Prix "2019 Canadian Grand Prix"), Verstappen's final lap in the second qualifying session was hampered by a red flag brought out by [Kevin Magnussen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Magnussen "Kevin Magnussen")'s crash. This caused Verstappen to qualify 11th and start the race in ninth place.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-138)[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-139) He later recovered to finish fifth.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-140) In [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_French_Grand_Prix "2019 French Grand Prix") he started and finished in fourth place.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-141) In [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2019 Austrian Grand Prix"), Verstappen started third but suffered a poor start, dropping down to eighth. After a charge towards the front, he made his way up to second before controversially passing Leclerc for the lead of the race with three laps to go.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-142) This marked the first Honda-powered race victory since the [2006 Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2006 Hungarian Grand Prix").[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-143)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-144) In [Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_British_Grand_Prix "2019 British Grand Prix"), Verstappen, running in third place,[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-145) was hit from behind during an overtake attempt by Sebastian Vettel and spun into the gravel. Verstappen was able to continue and crossed the line in fifth place.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-146)
The wet and chaotic [German Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_German_Grand_Prix "2019 German Grand Prix") began similarly to the race in Austria for Verstappen, as a poor start caused him to fall behind. However, he would inherit the lead midway through the race after a crash by race leader Hamilton.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-147) Verstappen would go on to extend his lead after the track began to dry, claiming his second victory of the season.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-148) In [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2019 Hungarian Grand Prix"), he claimed his maiden [pole position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_polesitters "List of Formula One polesitters")—becoming the [first Dutch driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_the_Netherlands "Formula One drivers from the Netherlands") to do so—and led most of the race before being passed in the closing laps by Hamilton, who had made another stop for fresh tyres in a gamble to catch the leader.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-149)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-150)[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-151)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e0/F%C3%B3rmula_1_%E2%80%93_Grande_Pr%C3%AAmio_do_Brasil_de_F1_2019_%2849080565726%29.jpg/250px-F%C3%B3rmula_1_%E2%80%93_Grande_Pr%C3%AAmio_do_Brasil_de_F1_2019_%2849080565726%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:F%C3%B3rmula_1_%E2%80%93_Grande_Pr%C3%AAmio_do_Brasil_de_F1_2019_\(49080565726\).jpg)Verstappen on the podium after winning the [2019 Brazilian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Brazilian_Grand_Prix "2019 Brazilian Grand Prix")
Before the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2019 Belgian Grand Prix"), Verstappen received a new teammate in Alexander Albon after Pierre Gasly was demoted back to Toro Rosso.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-152) In the race, Verstappen had a poor start and collided with Kimi Räikkönen at the first corner, resulting in suspension damage and causing Verstappen's first retirement of the season.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-153) In [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Italian_Grand_Prix "2019 Italian Grand Prix"), he did not set a time during qualifying after his car lost power in Q1, but he was already required to start from the back of the grid due to an engine component penalty.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-154) After damaging his front wing on the first lap, he recovered to finish the race in eighth place.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-155) Third and fourth-place finishes followed in [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2019 Singapore Grand Prix") and [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Russian_Grand_Prix "2019 Russian Grand Prix") respectively.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-156)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-157) After suffering damage in a first-lap collision with Charles Leclerc in [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2019 Japanese Grand Prix"), Verstappen suffered his second retirement of the season.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-158)
In [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Mexican_Grand_Prix "2019 Mexican Grand Prix"), he qualified in first place after setting the fastest lap-time of the session, before being handed a grid penalty for ignoring [yellow flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_flags#Yellow_flag "Racing flags") after a crash by Valtteri Bottas.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-159) Verstappen suffered a puncture early in the race after making contact with Bottas, falling to the back of the field before eventually recovering to sixth place.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-160) A third-place finish in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_United_States_Grand_Prix "2019 United States Grand Prix") followed, before Verstappen took the second pole position of his career with a 1:07.508 pole lap time in [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Brazilian_Grand_Prix "2019 Brazilian Grand Prix").[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-161)[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-162) In a chaotic race, he passed Lewis Hamilton for the lead on two occasions before going on to claim his third victory of the season.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-163) Verstappen ended the season with a second-place finish in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2019 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix").[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-164) Verstappen finished the 2019 season in third place in the championship with 278 points. He claimed three race victories, nine podium finishes, two pole positions, and three fastest laps.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-165)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c0/Max_Verstappen%2C_2020_pre-season_testing.jpg/250px-Max_Verstappen%2C_2020_pre-season_testing.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Max_Verstappen,_2020_pre-season_testing.jpg)Verstappen at [pre-season testing in 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Formula_One_pre-season_testing "2020 Formula One pre-season testing")
Verstappen continued to race for Red Bull in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Formula_One_World_Championship "2020 Formula One World Championship"), alongside Albon. At the [2020 Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2020 Austrian Grand Prix"), he started second, but retired early in the race after a flywheel-related problem caused an electronic issue within the power unit.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-166) Honda introduced countermeasures in response to the retirement.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-167) At the [2020 Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2020 Hungarian Grand Prix"), he crashed in wet conditions during the [formation lap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_lap "Formation lap") while he was on his way to the starting grid,[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-168) but he was able to drive the car back to the grid where his mechanics fixed the suspension of the car in the short time that was left before the start of the race.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-169) After the repairs, Verstappen progressed from seventh place on the grid to second place by the end of the race.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-170) Verstappen won the [70th Anniversary Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/70th_Anniversary_Grand_Prix "70th Anniversary Grand Prix") at [Silverstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverstone_Circuit "Silverstone Circuit"), having started from fourth.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-MVvolgensGR-171)
Verstappen clinched second place at the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2020 Spanish Grand Prix"), after qualifying in third.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-172) At the [2020 Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2020 Belgian Grand Prix"), he scored a podium in third place, following his third place on the starting grid.[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-173) He suffered from two consecutive DNFs at the [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Italian_Grand_Prix "2020 Italian Grand Prix") and [Tuscan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Tuscan_Grand_Prix "2020 Tuscan Grand Prix") Grands Prix after which he lost second place in the Championship.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-174)[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-175) At the [Russian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Russian_Grand_Prix "2020 Russian Grand Prix"), Verstappen finished the race in second, his seventh podium finish of 2020.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-176) At the [Eifel Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Eifel_Grand_Prix "2020 Eifel Grand Prix"), Verstappen finished in second after qualifying in third.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-177) He also managed to get the fastest lap of the race.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-178) At the [Portuguese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Portuguese_Grand_Prix "2020 Portuguese Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified third, however a poor first lap meant that he dropped back down the order to fifth place. He recovered to third and took his 40th podium in Formula 1.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-179) At the [Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "2020 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix"), Verstappen looked set to claim second due to [Valtteri Bottas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valtteri_Bottas "Valtteri Bottas")' ailing Mercedes slowing down, but a sudden puncture denied him any chance of a podium finish; Verstappen spun, resulting in his fourth retirement of the 2020 season.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-180)
During Free Practice for the Portuguese Grand Prix, Verstappen was criticised for comments he made on the team radio after a collision with [Lance Stroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Stroll "Lance Stroll"), where he used the words "retard" and "mongol" in response to the clash. Verstappen admitted following the session that the word choices he used were "not correct". The Mongolian government and the Mongol identity asked Verstappen to apologise for the comments; the Mongolian government also urged the [FIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l'Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile") to take action on the comments he made.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-181)[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-182) Verstappen finished the 2020 season in third place in the championship with 214 points. He claimed two race victories, eleven podium finishes, one pole position, and three fastest laps.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-183)
#### 2021: Successful title battle with Hamilton
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/FIA_F1_Austria_2021_Nr._33_Verstappen.jpg/250px-FIA_F1_Austria_2021_Nr._33_Verstappen.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FIA_F1_Austria_2021_Nr._33_Verstappen.jpg)Verstappen at the 2021 Austrian Grand Prix
Verstappen won his first F1 championship in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship"). At the [Bahrain Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2021 Bahrain Grand Prix"), Verstappen topped all the practice sessions and subsequently took a career fourth pole position. This was the first time he achieved back-to-back pole positions.[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-184) He fought Lewis Hamilton for the race victory, and on lap 53 Verstappen overtook Hamilton, but went off track whilst doing so, resulting in him being instructed by race control to let Hamilton back into the lead and ultimately finishing second behind Hamilton.[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-185) At the next race, the [Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "2021 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified third with teammate [Sergio Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_P%C3%A9rez "Sergio Pérez") second, marking the first time he was out-qualified by a teammate since the [2019 Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Italian_Grand_Prix "2019 Italian Grand Prix").[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-186) At the race start, Verstappen was able to pass both Pérez and pole-sitter Hamilton to take the lead. He remained in the lead after the first round of pit stops as well as the restart, following the race being suspended on lap 33. Rival Hamilton finished second, reducing his championship lead over Verstappen to one point.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-187)
In the following [Portuguese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Portuguese_Grand_Prix "2021 Portuguese Grand Prix"), Verstappen finished second after a long battle with Hamilton.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-188) At the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2021 Spanish Grand Prix"), the battle between Verstappen and Hamilton continued, with Hamilton employing a faster two-stop strategy versus Verstappen's one-stop race. This provided Hamilton the advantage of faster tyres, allowing him to overtake Verstappen with several laps remaining in the race. Hamilton took the victory, with Verstappen taking second and the fastest lap, increasing Hamilton's championship lead to 14 points.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-189)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Suzuka_Fan_Thanksgiving_Day_2022_%2836%29_-_RedBull_Honda_RB16-01_in_2022_Formula_1.jpg/330px-Suzuka_Fan_Thanksgiving_Day_2022_%2836%29_-_RedBull_Honda_RB16-01_in_2022_Formula_1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Suzuka_Fan_Thanksgiving_Day_2022_\(36\)_-_RedBull_Honda_RB16-01_in_2022_Formula_1.jpg)Verstappen's 2021 title winning [RB16B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB16B "RB16B") in [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") colors white and red, as a tribute to their engine supplier [Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda "Honda")
At the next race in [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2021 Monaco Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified second behind [Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc"),[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-190) but Leclerc suffered a driveshaft failure on the way to the grid and was unable to start the race. Verstappen controlled the race from the front on the way to victory. Hamilton (who qualified seventh) finished seventh, though claiming an extra championship point by setting the fastest race lap. The result enabled Verstappen to become the [first Dutch driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_the_Netherlands "Formula One drivers from the Netherlands") to lead the World Drivers' Championship,[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-191) by a margin of four points over Hamilton.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-192) At the [Azerbaijan Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2021 Azerbaijan Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified third behind Leclerc and Hamilton.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-193) Verstappen and Hamilton passed Leclerc in the opening laps before Verstappen took the lead by way of a faster pitstop. Verstappen would comfortably hold the lead until lap 46 when he suffered a tyre failure causing him to crash at high speed and retire.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-194) A mistake by Hamilton on the restart dropped him to last place, meaning Verstappen maintained his championship lead.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-195)
Verstappen took pole for the [French Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_French_Grand_Prix "2021 French Grand Prix").[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-196) Verstappen's mistake on the first lap allowed Hamilton to take the lead which Verstappen retook during the pit stop phase. Verstappen pitted for a second time from the lead and set after the Mercedes duo, overtaking Hamilton for the lead on lap 52 of 53.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-197) He also took the fastest lap point, extending his championship lead to twelve points[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-198) and achieving the first [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Pole,_win,_and_fastest_lap_in_same_race "List of Formula One driver records") of his career.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-199) Verstappen clinched pole position again at the [Styrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Styrian_Grand_Prix "2021 Styrian Grand Prix") and led the race from start to finish, to give him his fourth win of the season and further extend his lead to 18 points.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-200)
Verstappen took pole position at the [Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2021 Austrian Grand Prix"), led every lap from start to finish, set the fastest lap, and won the race for his first career [grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_\(Formula_One\) "Grand slam \(Formula One\)"),[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-:6-201)[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-202) being the youngest to do so.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-203) With the win, Verstappen also became the first driver to win three races in three consecutive weekends, starting at the French Grand Prix on 20 June, then the Styrian Grand Prix on 27 June and ending with the Austrian Grand Prix on 4 July.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-204)[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-205) At the next race; the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_British_Grand_Prix "2021 British Grand Prix"), Verstappen was involved in a high-speed collision at the _[Copse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silverstone_Circuit#Circuit "Silverstone Circuit")_ corner with Hamilton on the first lap. This resulted in a 51 [_g_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G-force "G-force") (500 [m/s2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metre_per_second_squared "Metre per second squared"); 1,600 [ft/s2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot_per_second_squared "Foot per second squared")) impact with the barrier.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-206)[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-207) He was taken to the Silverstone circuit's medical centre after the crash and was then taken to Coventry hospital for precautionary checks and further assessment, before eventually being discharged at 22:00 local time on Sunday night.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-208) Hamilton would go on to win the race, reducing Verstappen's lead in the championship to eight points.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-209) At the next race, the [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2021 Hungarian Grand Prix"), Verstappen's car suffered damage in a multi-car collision on lap 1, where Mercedes driver Valtteri Bottas was deemed at fault. He ended the race in tenth which was promoted to ninth after Sebastian Vettel was disqualified. The outcome of the race allowed Hamilton to take the lead of the championship.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-210)
Following the summer break, Verstappen qualified on pole at the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2021 Belgian Grand Prix"), ahead of Williams driver [George Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Russell_\(racing_driver\) "George Russell \(racing driver\)") in second and Lewis Hamilton in third.[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-211) The race was run for three laps, all behind the safety car, with the race official race results taken from the running order at the end of the first lap, with Hamilton and Verstappen both retaining their qualifying positions. As less than 75% of the race distance was completed, half points were awarded, resulting in Verstappen closing the gap to Hamilton to three points.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-212) At the [Dutch Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Dutch_Grand_Prix "2021 Dutch Grand Prix") Verstappen again qualified on pole, beating Hamilton by 0.038 seconds.[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-213) During the race Verstappen was able to fend off attacks from both Mercedes drivers to take the win, taking the lead in the Drivers' Championship by three points.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-RedBull.com-214) For the [Russian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Russian_Grand_Prix "2021 Russian Grand Prix"), Verstappen was required to start at the back of the grid for exceeding his quota of power unit components.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-215) He made his way back up the field, and after taking an early pit stop for intermediate tyres late in the race, he finished second.[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-216) At the [Turkish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Turkish_Grand_Prix "2021 Turkish Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified second with Bottas on pole.[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-217) With the race being run in wet conditions and the drivers on intermediate tyres the whole race, Verstappen finished second behind Bottas, taking the lead in the Drivers' Championship by six points as Hamilton finished fifth.[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-218)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/2021_United_States_Grand_Prix_23_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-2021_United_States_Grand_Prix_23_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2021_United_States_Grand_Prix_23_\(cropped\).jpg)Verstappen battling with Lewis Hamilton for the lead at the 2021 United States Grand Prix
