At the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_United_States_Grand_Prix "2021 United States Grand Prix"), Verstappen took pole position in qualifying, edging Hamilton by 0.209 seconds.[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-219) Verstappen won the race and extended his lead in the Drivers' Championship to twelve points as Hamilton finished second with the fastest lap.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-BBC_Sport_2021-220) At the [2021 Mexico City Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Mexico_City_Grand_Prix "2021 Mexico City Grand Prix"), Verstappen qualified third with a gap to pole-sitter Bottas of 0.350 seconds.[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-221) Verstappen's main rival Hamilton qualified second. At the start, Verstappen took the lead from Bottas and Hamilton into turn 1, and won the race; and as a result extended his lead in the championship to 19 points.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Fox_Sports_2021-222)
Verstappen and Hamilton each entered the final round of the championship—the [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix") at [Yas Marina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yas_Marina_Circuit "Yas Marina Circuit")—on exactly 369.5 points, with Verstappen leading on countback.[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-223) Verstappen qualified on pole position by nearly four-tenths of a second, but had a slow start and lost the lead to Hamilton into turn one.[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-224) He attempted to re-pass Hamilton at turn six, who cut the track but was not penalised and maintained the lead. The stewards deemed that no advantage was gained, amidst Verstappen's and Red Bull's complaints.[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-225) Verstappen was trailing Hamilton by over 10 seconds until a safety car was deployed with five laps remaining.[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-226) The ending of the safety car and subsequent resumption of the race for one single lap caused significant controversy; race director [Michael Masi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Masi "Michael Masi") allowed all lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen to unlap themselves, but no other. He also restarted the race for the next lap in supposed contravention to the rulebook.[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-227) Verstappen passed Hamilton at turn five of the final lap of the final race to become the [first World Drivers' Champion from the Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_the_Netherlands "Formula One drivers from the Netherlands") and the [34th overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Drivers'_Championship "World Drivers' Championship").[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-228)[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-229) Mercedes' protests were dismissed by the stewards[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-230) and Verstappen was provisionally confirmed as world champion, pending any appeal. Having initially lodged their intention, Mercedes later decided not to submit an appeal of the race results. Verstappen was named the best driver of the season by _[Autosport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosport "Autosport")_ and _The Race_ ,[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-231)[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-232) whilst also topping polls of fellow drivers and team principals.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-233)[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-234) [Mark Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Hughes_\(journalist\) "Mark Hughes \(journalist\)") of _[Motor Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_Sport_\(magazine\) "Motor Sport \(magazine\)")_ also ranked Verstappen first, describing his season as a "stunning combination of speed and racecraft, totally fearless, incredible tenacity and ability to comeback from adversity".[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-235)
#### 2022: Defending the championship
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/RB18_JapaneseGP_FP2.jpg/250px-RB18_JapaneseGP_FP2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RB18_JapaneseGP_FP2.jpg)Verstappen at the [2022 Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2022 Japanese Grand Prix"), where he won his second World Drivers' Championship
In March 2022, Verstappen signed a five-year contract extension with Red Bull Racing for the 2023 to 2028 seasons.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-:3-236) From this season onward, he would use the number 1 instead of his regular number 33 as the reigning world champion.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-237) Verstappen retired from second place at the [season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Formula_One_World_Championship "2022 Formula One World Championship")-opening [Bahrain Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2022 Bahrain Grand Prix") with a fuel system issue. He won the [Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2022 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix"), having benefited from a pit stop during safety car conditions to pass teammate and pole-sitter Pérez, but suffered another fuel-related retirement from second place at the [Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Australian_Grand_Prix "2022 Australian Grand Prix"). This left him 46 points behind championship leader Charles Leclerc after three races. Verstappen won the next three races; including sprint victory and a [grand slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_slam_\(Formula_One\) "Grand slam \(Formula One\)") at the [Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "2022 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix"),[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-238) won from third on the grid at the [Miami Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Miami_Grand_Prix "2022 Miami Grand Prix") while profiting from Leclerc's retirement at the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2022 Spanish Grand Prix") to take the championship lead. Further wins came at the [Azerbaijan Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2022 Azerbaijan Grand Prix"), where Leclerc again retired, and from pole position at the [Canadian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Canadian_Grand_Prix "2022 Canadian Grand Prix"). Verstappen qualified second at the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_British_Grand_Prix "2022 British Grand Prix"), but floor damage from running over debris harmed his pace and resulted in a seventh-place finish.[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-239)
Verstappen took pole position at the [Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2022 Austrian Grand Prix") and won the sprint, but was overtaken by Leclerc in the race and finished second, reducing his championship lead over Leclerc to 38 points. Following this, Verstappen went on to win five races consecutively. Pole-sitter Leclerc crashed out of the [French Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_French_Grand_Prix "2022 French Grand Prix"), allowing Verstappen to win. Power unit issues meant he qualified tenth for the [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2022 Hungarian Grand Prix"),[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-240) but overtakes in the opening laps and pit stop [undercuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_motorsport_terms#U "Glossary of motorsport terms") meant he went on to take victory, despite briefly losing the lead after a spin.[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-241) He set the fastest qualifying time at the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2022 Belgian Grand Prix") but was demoted to 14th on the grid with a power unit components penalty. Despite this, he progressed to the race lead by lap 12 and went on to win.[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-belg2022-242) He took pole position and his 30th race victory at his home race, the [Dutch Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Dutch_Grand_Prix "2022 Dutch Grand Prix"), and then won from seventh on the grid at the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Italian_Grand_Prix "2022 Italian Grand Prix").
Verstappen's winning streak was ended at the [Singapore Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2022 Singapore Grand Prix"). He ran out of fuel in qualifying and started the race eighth.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-243) He lost places at the start and later had to make an extra pit stop due to a tyre lock-up, finishing seventh. Victory from pole at the shortened [Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2022 Japanese Grand Prix") gave him a 113-point lead in the standings with four races remaining, securing him his second World Drivers' Championship.[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Morlidge_2022-244) He won the next two races, the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_United_States_Grand_Prix "2022 United States Grand Prix") and [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Mexico_City_Grand_Prix "2022 Mexico City Grand Prix") Grands Prix, finished sixth at the [São Paulo Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2022 São Paulo Grand Prix") after a collision with Lewis Hamilton, and won the season-ending [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2022 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix") from pole. Abu Dhabi was his fifteenth victory of the year, breaking the record of thirteen race wins in a season shared by Michael Schumacher in [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Formula_One_World_Championship "2004 Formula One World Championship") and Sebastian Vettel in [2013](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_Formula_One_World_Championship "2013 Formula One World Championship"). He won the championship with 454 points, beating Lewis Hamilton's [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Formula_One_World_Championship "2019 Formula One World Championship") record of 413.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-245)
#### 2023: Record-breaking third title
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/FIA_F1_Austria_2023_Race_%281%29.jpg/250px-FIA_F1_Austria_2023_Race_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FIA_F1_Austria_2023_Race_\(1\).jpg)Verstappen leading the race at the [2023 Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2023 Austrian Grand Prix")
Verstappen remained with Red Bull alongside Sergio Pérez for the [2023 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship"). His campaign began with a win from pole at the [Bahrain Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2023 Bahrain Grand Prix"). A driveshaft failure in qualifying at the [Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2023 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix") resulted in a 15th-place start, but he gained positions in the race to finish second behind Pérez.[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-246) He again won from pole at the [Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Australian_Grand_Prix "2023 Australian Grand Prix") despite losing positions to the Mercedes drivers during the race,[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Sky_Sports_-_wild_finish-247) but finished second to Pérez, who made a safety car pit stop, at the [Azerbaijan Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2023 Azerbaijan Grand Prix").[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-248)
After this began Verstappen's record-breaking win streak. He started ninth at the [Miami Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Miami_Grand_Prix "2023 Miami Grand Prix") as [red flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_flags#Red_flag "Racing flags") in qualifying aborted his lap but passed the drivers ahead including pole-sitter Pérez to win. The next four races, the [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2023 Monaco Grand Prix"), [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2023 Spanish Grand Prix"), [Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Canadian_Grand_Prix "2023 Canadian Grand Prix") and [Austrian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2023 Austrian Grand Prix") Grands Prix, were won comfortably from pole position by Verstappen, including Red Bull's 100th victory in Canada,[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-249) as well as a sprint win in Austria. He took pole at the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_British_Grand_Prix "2023 British Grand Prix") but briefly lost the lead to [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris") at the start before regaining the position to win. He qualified 0.003 seconds behind Lewis Hamilton at the [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2023 Hungarian Grand Prix"), but overtook him at the first corner and went on to take victory. He claimed pole and the win in the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2023 Belgian Grand Prix") sprint and set the fastest qualifying time, but started the race sixth due to an engine component penalty. He went on to overtake Pérez to win the race. He won from pole at the rain-affected [Dutch Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Dutch_Grand_Prix "2023 Dutch Grand Prix") and was victorious again at the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Italian_Grand_Prix "2023 Italian Grand Prix") despite qualifying behind Carlos Sainz Jr. This victory marked his tenth consecutive win, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record of nine from 2013,[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-250)[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-251) and Red Bull's fifteenth consecutive win, a record previously held by [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren") with eleven in [1988](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Formula_One_World_Championship "1988 Formula One World Championship"). Both Red Bulls were eliminated in Q2 at the [Singapore Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2023 Singapore Grand Prix") and were unable to make an impression in the race, with Verstappen and Pérez finishing fifth and eighth respectively, ending the winning streak.[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-252) This would be the only break in Verstappen's success, as he went on to win the remaining seven races of the season. His victory from pole at the [Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2023 Japanese Grand Prix") gave Red Bull their sixth Constructors' Championship title.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-253)
Verstappen clinched his third World Drivers' Championship title at the [Qatar Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Qatar_Grand_Prix "2023 Qatar Grand Prix") sprint despite finishing second to [Oscar Piastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Piastri "Oscar Piastri"),[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-254) then won the race from pole. He won the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_United_States_Grand_Prix "2023 United States Grand Prix") despite having started sixth due to a lap time deletion in qualifying. He qualified behind both Ferraris at the [Mexico City Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Mexico_City_Grand_Prix "2023 Mexico City Grand Prix") but passed both drivers to claim the win. He took pole and victory at the [São Paulo Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2023 São Paulo Grand Prix") and won the sprint having overtook pole-sitter [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris") at the first turn. He started behind Charles Leclerc at the [Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "2023 Las Vegas Grand Prix") and received a penalty for forcing him off the track, but Verstappen reclaimed the lead to win. His pole and victory at the season-ending [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2023 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix") was his nineteenth win of the year, breaking his own record of fifteen from 2022. He scored 575 points, more than double that of second-placed Pérez and beating his own points-scoring record from 2022.
#### 2024: Fourth title despite Red Bull struggles

Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2024 Bahrain Grand Prix")[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-255) and followed this with another pole and Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2024 Japanese Grand Prix").[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-258) He won the sprint at the [Chinese Verstappen and George Russell set identical lap times in qualifying at the [Canadian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Canadian_Grand_Prix "2024 Canadian Grand Prix"), but Russell started on pole position as he had set the lap time first.[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-265) Both drivers were overtaken by Norris, but Verstappen later passed Russell then gained the lead from Norris during the pit stops to claim his 60th race win.[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-266) He qualified second behind Norris at the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2024 Spanish Grand Prix") but passed him at the start and then overtook Russell to win for the seventh time in 2024.[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-267) Verstappen won the sprint from pole at the [Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2024 Austrian Grand Prix")[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-268) and then qualified fastest for the main race.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-269) He led most of the race but was challenged by Norris in the closing laps before the two drivers collided; Verstappen was handed a time penalty for causing the collision and finished the race fifth.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-270) He later commented that the crash did not affect his close friendship with Norris.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-271) He qualified fourth at the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_British_Grand_Prix "2024 British Grand Prix") and passed Norris in the closing laps to finish second behind Lewis Hamilton.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-272) He started third at the [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2024 Hungarian Grand Prix") but collided with Hamilton and went on to finish fifth. He criticised his team's race strategy and suggested that the RB20 was now behind the race-winning [McLaren MCL38](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MCL38 "McLaren MCL38") on pace.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-273) Verstappen qualified fastest at the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2024 Belgian Grand Prix") but started outside the top ten due to an engine component penalty.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-274) He recovered positions and was classified fourth in the race,[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-275) extending his lead in the championship to 78 points over Norris going into the summer break.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-276)

corner, but was later overtaken by Norris and finished second.[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-277) He qualified and finished outside the top four at both the [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Italian_Grand_Prix "2024 Italian Grand Prix") and [Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2024 Azerbaijan Grand Prix") official press conference in Singapore, for which he received a punishment from the FIA to "accomplish some work of public interest".[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-281) Verstappen was classified fourth in the [São Paulo Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2024 São Paulo Grand Prix") sprint after receiving a [virtual safety car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virtual_safety_car "Virtual safety car") infringement penalty,[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-287) and started the race from 17th following an engine penalty, whilst Norris qualified on pole. He gained seven positions on the opening lap, with further places obtained via several crucial overtakes, as well as surviving the worsening conditions on his intermediate tyres until the [red flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_flags#Red_flag "Racing flags") period.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-288) Following this—and his overtake for the lead on Ocon—Verstappen set ten of the eleven fastest laps of the race, with his quickest being 1.045 seconds quicker than any of his rivals;[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-289) he won by a 19-second margin, increasing his championship lead to 62 points.[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-SP24stat-290) Verstappen was lauded by drivers and critics for his drive;[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-291)[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-292)[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-293) Giles Richards of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ opined that his performance was "worthy of recognition in the [pantheon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantheon_\(religion\) "Pantheon \(religion\)") of Formula One's wet-weather drives", describing him as a _[regenmeister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regenmeister_\(disambiguation\) "Regenmeister \(disambiguation\)")_ (lit. 'rain master').[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-294) By finishing ahead of Norris at the subsequent [Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix"), Verstappen secured his fourth world title with two races remaining.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-295) Winning eight Grands Prix in all, Andrew Benson of _[BBC Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sport "BBC Sport")_ proclaimed it as a "towering achievement from a driver recognised as one of the all-time greats of Formula 1", describing his season as "almost flawless" whilst "not [having] the best car for the majority".[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-296) Verstappen won the [Qatar Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Qatar_Grand_Prix "2024 Qatar Grand Prix"), leading every lap after having his pole position stripped for driving unnecessarily slowly in qualifying; the incident led to a widely publicised feud with [George Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Russell_\(racing_driver\) "George Russell \(racing driver\)"). After the season-ending [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"), Verstappen became the first driver to win a title driving for a third-placed team in the [World Constructors' Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Constructors'_Championship "World Constructors' Championship") since [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") in [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Formula_One_World_Championship "1983 Formula One World Championship").[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-297)

Finishing fourth from sixth at the [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2025 São Paulo Grand Prix") sprint, Verstappen qualified sixteenth for the Grand Prix, his lowest qualifying position – excluding any penalties – since the [2021 Russian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Russian_Grand_Prix "2021 Russian Grand Prix"), which he chose not to run any qualifying laps for due to impending engine and grid penalties. Red Bull started him from the pit lane after changing his engine in _[parc fermé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_ferm%C3%A9 "Parc fermé")_ ; surviving an early puncture, he climbed up to third in the race to draw ever closer to the championship lead. Verstappen won at [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix") with both McLarens being disqualified post-race, moving him level on points with Piastri and 24 behind championship leader Norris. Verstappen finished fourth in the [Qatar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Qatar_Grand_Prix "2025 Qatar Grand Prix") sprint before improving to collect a win in the Grand Prix, bringing him twelve points behind Norris and overtaking Piastri for second in the championship. Converting pole position in [Abu Dhabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2025 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix") to a win, he achieved the most Grand Prix wins throughout the season with eight overall, with both McLaren drivers winning seven apiece. He ultimately placed merely two points behind Norris, who secured the Drivers' Championship.

## Driver profile
### Qualifying pace and consistency
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/30/2018_Chinese_Grand_Prix_Qualifying_Max_Verstappen_%2827842985498%29.jpg/250px-2018_Chinese_Grand_Prix_Qualifying_Max_Verstappen_%2827842985498%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2018_Chinese_Grand_Prix_Qualifying_Max_Verstappen_\(27842985498\).jpg)Verstappen on a qualifying lap at the [2018 Chinese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2018 Chinese Grand Prix")
Following Verstappen's maiden pole position at the 2019 Hungarian Grand Prix, former Formula One World Champion Nico Rosberg described him as the fastest driver in Formula One. Rosberg elucidated that Verstappen did not have the fastest car during the qualifying session in Hungary, emphasising that it was Verstappen's raw speed that allowed him to secure pole position: "Mercedes still had the fastest car, and it's just Verstappen with his driving that put it up there in pole."[[345]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-348)
In 2019, former Formula One World Champion [Jenson Button](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenson_Button "Jenson Button") stated that he believes Verstappen is the fastest Formula One driver ever: "I think he is the fastest driver that has ever driven an F1 car. I really do, I think he is unbelievably fast."[[346]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-349) Journalist Scott Mitchell from _The Race_ commented: "When everything comes together, Verstappen is the quickest driver in F1 over one lap, but the odd mistake and scruffy session must be eliminated."[[347]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-350) Helmut Marko, the advisor to the [Red Bull GmbH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_GmbH "Red Bull GmbH") Formula One teams, stated that Verstappen is the fastest driver Red Bull have ever had.[[348]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-351)[[349]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-352)
In 2021, three-time Formula One World Champion [Jackie Stewart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Stewart "Jackie Stewart") claimed that Verstappen is the fastest driver in Formula One, but he also added that Verstappen is still in the "puppy stage" of his career.[[350]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-353) [Peter Windsor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Windsor "Peter Windsor"), an experienced Formula One journalist, expressed Verstappen's ability to change direction "quicker than anybody else" through the high-speed section Maggots and Becketts: Silverstone's fastest sequence of corners. Windsor stressed that Verstappen's lightning-quick change of direction is a result of the innate feel he has for creating the "perfect platform" to achieve what he wants with the car during a lap. He is intrinsically able to create, for "a trillionth of a second", a minuscule "flat area" between the left and the right of a change of direction ahead of him, in order to attain a stable balance with the car before applying the next steering and throttle input.[[351]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-354) [Scuderia AlphaTauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_AlphaTauri "Scuderia AlphaTauri")'s team principal, [Franz Tost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Tost "Franz Tost"), declared Verstappen to be the fastest driver in Formula One; following the Dutchman's "really deserved" maiden title triumph in 2021.[[352]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Woodhouse2021-355) After winning the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship "2024 Formula One World Championship") World Drivers' Championship in the third-placed [RB20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_RB20 "Red Bull RB20"), James Elson of _[Motor Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_Sport_\(magazine\) "Motor Sport \(magazine\)")_ stated "if there was any doubt beforehand, 2024 proved that Max Verstappen is F1's best driver", adding that "not only the fastest, capable of creating one-lap magic, he knows how to produce all it takes to win in the race too".[[353]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-356) Verstappen received widespread acclaim for his surprise pole lap at the [2025 Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2025 Japanese Grand Prix"),[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-JPN2025-301) with Andrew Benson of _[BBC Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sport "BBC Sport")_ commenting that "many F1 observers regarded [Verstappen's qualifying lap] as one of the greatest of all time".[[354]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-357)
### Dominance over teammates
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Red_Bull_duo_2016_Malaysia_Race.jpg/250px-Red_Bull_duo_2016_Malaysia_Race.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Red_Bull_duo_2016_Malaysia_Race.jpg)Verstappen _(right)_ was teammates with [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") _(left)_ from [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Formula_One_World_Championship "2016 Formula One World Championship") to [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Formula_One_World_Championship "2018 Formula One World Championship"), pictured at the [2016 Malaysian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2016 Malaysian Grand Prix").
Former Formula One driver [Eddie Irvine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Irvine "Eddie Irvine") praised Verstappen, stating that he is "by far the most dominant team leader on the grid." Irvine highlighted that Verstappen "has had many different second drivers in the team and none of them have got close to him."[[355]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Sharan2021Irvine-358) During the 2020 season, Jenson Button stated that he does not "think there's been a driver that's annihilated their teammates like he [Verstappen] has in a very long time."[[356]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-359) Motorsport columnist and former Formula One driver [Jolyon Palmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolyon_Palmer "Jolyon Palmer"), commented that Verstappen's maiden World Championship triumph could usher in a "new era of dominance" in the sport. Palmer wrote:
> [Verstappen's] qualifying pace is frightening and has been the basis for this title-charging campaign. He's had the most pole positions of anyone with 10 – almost half of the races, and it would have been half had he completed his mesmeric Jeddah lap, which ended up being possibly Max's biggest error in a near-perfect season. For a driver who has demolished three successive team mates in three years and made only a handful of small mistakes in that time, you question what scope their [_[sic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sic "Sic")_] even is for improvement – but if he can take his game onto another level from here, we could be about to see the start of a new era of dominance.[[357]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-360)
Journalist Scott Mitchell expounded the reason why the Dutchman's teammates have fallen short "even with the data". Mitchell wrote: "Verstappen drives mainly on intuition, and that comes from years of training and preparation. He has a database in his head which he can use immediately. Even with data, Gasly and Albon could see where he was faster, but they could never grasp how he was faster there. That's because what makes Verstappen so good is mainly unconscious." According to Mitchell, those years of training and driving on his intuition has made it impossible for other drivers to measure up to Verstappen.[[358]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-361)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Verstappen_%26_Perez_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg/250px-Verstappen_%26_Perez_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Verstappen_&_Perez_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg)Verstappen _(right)_ was teammates with [Sergio Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_P%C3%A9rez "Sergio Pérez") _(left)_ from 2021 to 2024, pictured at the [2024 Chinese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2024 Chinese Grand Prix").
Helmut Marko asserted that Verstappen's progress has moved him clear of his former Formula 1 team-mate Daniel Ricciardo, in both qualifying and race trim. "There is specific data," Marko told _Autosport_ , "In qualifying the gap to Ricciardo is greater. The strange thing is Max sometimes slides more, but still manages to keep the tyres alive." Verstappen previously mentioned that he was three or four-tenths faster on average than "very fast qualifier" Daniel Ricciardo.[[359]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-362) Marko concluded that then 20-year-old Verstappen "clearly moved away" from Ricciardo since the "second half of the 2018 season."[[360]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-363)

Verstappen's four championship-winning cars from top-to-bottom: [RB16B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_RB16B "Red Bull RB16B") ([2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship")), [RB18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_RB18 "Red Bull RB18") ([2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Formula_One_World_Championship "2022 Formula One World Championship")), [RB19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_RB19 "Red Bull RB19") ([2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship")) and [RB20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_RB20 "Red Bull RB20") ([2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship "2024 Formula One World Championship"))
Following his maiden Formula One win, at the [2016 Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2016 Spanish Grand Prix"), three-time World Drivers' Champion [Niki Lauda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niki_Lauda "Niki Lauda") described Verstappen as the "talent of the century".[[361]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-364) Red Bull team principal Christian Horner stated that Verstappen is the best driver Red Bull have ever seen: "I have no doubt [Verstappen is] the best we have seen on one of our cars, in terms of outright raw ability and commitment. He's the best driver we've seen."[[362]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-365)
[Gerhard Berger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Berger "Gerhard Berger") echoed [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Formula_One_World_Championship "2009 Formula One World Championship") World Drivers' Champion [Jenson Button](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jenson_Button "Jenson Button")'s comments, anointing Max Verstappen as the Formula One driver of this era with the most raw talent. Speaking to _Sport1_ , Berger ventured: "When it comes to raw talent, Max Verstappen is the most talented of all. But it's not just about raw talent, it's about the whole package. That means it's not just about setting the fastest laps but also to win a race. And not just [about] one race but many and eventually a championship, and championships."[[363]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-366)
Two-time World Drivers' Champion [Fernando Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Alonso "Fernando Alonso") commented that Verstappen is the standout driver in Formula One, declaring him to be "one step ahead" of everyone. Alonso noted that Verstappen deserved to win the [2021 Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship"), ahead of the title decider that saw Verstappen and [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") enter level on points: "Mercedes lately have been more performing and they've won a couple of races now, but Max is driving—in my opinion—one step ahead of all of us. We saw the [qualifying] lap in Jeddah, until he touched the wall at the last corner, that lap was coming from Max, not the Red Bull."[[364]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-367) [Karun Chandhok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karun_Chandhok "Karun Chandhok") likened Verstappen's ruthless and uncompromising attitude in race combat to seven-time World Drivers' Champion [Michael Schumacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Schumacher "Michael Schumacher").[[365]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-368) By [2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Formula_One_World_Championship "2025 Formula One World Championship"), Andrew Benson of _[BBC Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sport "BBC Sport")_ opined that Verstappen was "regarded by almost everyone in [Formula One] as the best driver in the world".[[366]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-369)

#### Lewis Hamilton
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/2022_French_Grand_Prix_%2852278980223%29.png/330px-2022_French_Grand_Prix_%2852278980223%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2022_French_Grand_Prix_\(52278980223\).png)Verstappen (left) and Hamilton (right) at the [2022 French Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_French_Grand_Prix "2022 French Grand Prix")
Verstappen's most well-known rival is his [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship") title rival, [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton").[[367]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-370)[[368]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-371) The title battle between Verstappen and Hamilton in 2021 has been compared to other legendary battles like the [Prost–Senna rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prost%E2%80%93Senna_rivalry "Prost–Senna rivalry").[[369]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-372) The two swapped leads five times, finished 1–2 in fourteen out of 22 races, and numerous incidents on-track involving the two[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-376) culminated in a title decider at the season finale, the [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"), where Verstappen, benefitting from newer tyres that were fitted during a safety car period, passed Hamilton on the final lap for the lead, and ultimately the championship.
#### Charles Leclerc
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e1/FIA_F1_Austria_2022_Podium_Race_%281%29.jpg/250px-FIA_F1_Austria_2022_Podium_Race_%281%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FIA_F1_Austria_2022_Podium_Race_\(1\).jpg)Verstappen (left), Leclerc (middle) and Hamilton (right) on the podium at the [2022 Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2022 Austrian Grand Prix")
[Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc") has also been cited as one of Verstappen's rivals. Following a [junior karting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing") incident in 2012 where Leclerc brushed off a collision with Verstappen as "just an incident", a rivalry began between the two which has since been matured into mutual respect. Verstappen's battles with Leclerc are characterised as cleaner and more respectful, focusing on "pure racing".[[373]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-377) Verstappen has noted he treats Leclerc differently than other rivals, simply because he has known him and trusted his racing ability.[[374]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-378)[[375]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-379) Verstappen and Leclerc battled for the championship at the beginning of [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Formula_One_World_Championship "2022 Formula One World Championship") before Ferrari's performance declined, allowing Red Bull and Verstappen to eventually secure both championships.
### Racecraft
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dd/Podium_2017_Malaysia.jpg/250px-Podium_2017_Malaysia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Podium_2017_Malaysia.jpg)Verstappen _(middle)_ on the podium with [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") _(left)_ and [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") _(right)_ after winning the [2017 Malaysian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Malaysian_Grand_Prix "2017 Malaysian Grand Prix")
Following Verstappen being given a warning for his driving conduct at the 2016 Belgian Grand Prix, the 18-year-old received the backing of then three-time champion Lewis Hamilton, who commented: "firstly, give the guy a break, he is 18 years old. What the frickin' heck were any of us doing at 18?"[[376]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-380)
Despite earning high praise and acclaim from Formula One drivers and experts in and out of the sport, Verstappen faced criticism in the wake of the penalties he incurred during the [2021 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2021 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix"). Following this race, former Formula One driver [Martin Brundle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Brundle "Martin Brundle") wrote: "Such is [his] car control and cunning, he's sometimes able to pull off the audacious moves and leave a margin of doubt as to whether it's hard racing or simply a professional foul outside of the regulations and it's those moments which are generating the confusion, controversies and inconsistencies. [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna") and Michael Schumacher had their faults too, and I was on the receiving end from both of them on occasions, but it's a sizeable dent on their immense reputations, not a positive."[[377]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-381) Following an impressive first half of the 2022 season, journalist [David Tremayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Tremayne "David Tremayne") claimed Verstappen had elevated himself to a new higher level compared to his 2021 title winning season, suggesting Verstappen's first title had made him more relaxed and "chirpy".[[378]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-382)
Following the [2024 Mexico City Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Mexico_City_Grand_Prix "2024 Mexico City Grand Prix"), Verstappen received widespread condemnation from fans and media for incidents involving title rival [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris"), for which he received 20 seconds worth of time penalties.[[379]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-383) Many commentators and former drivers likened his tactics and 'win-at-all-costs' attitude to those of Senna and Schumacher,[[380]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-384)[[381]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-385) whilst [1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Formula_One_World_Championship "1996 Formula One World Championship") World Drivers' Champion [Damon Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damon_Hill "Damon Hill") characterised them as reminiscent of _[Wacky Races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wacky_Races "Wacky Races")_ antagonist [Dick Dastardly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Dastardly "Dick Dastardly").[[382]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-386) Before the following race in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2024 São Paulo Grand Prix"), Verstappen criticised the alleged British bias in the media, stating "I have the wrong passport".[[383]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-387) Upon his victory from 17th on the grid in the rain-affected race, he stated in the post-race press conference "I appreciate all of you being here, but I don't see any British press. Do they have to run to the airport, or [do they not] know where the press conference is?"[[384]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-388)
### Fan support
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/FIA_F1_Austria_2021_Post-Race_Scene.jpg/250px-FIA_F1_Austria_2021_Post-Race_Scene.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:FIA_F1_Austria_2021_Post-Race_Scene.jpg)The Verstappen grandstand at the [2021 Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2021 Austrian Grand Prix")
Verstappen has accumulated a significant fanbase from around the world, particularly from his home country of the Netherlands. The frequent association of Verstappen with the colour [orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_\(colour\) "Orange \(colour\)")—the [national colour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_colour "National colour") of the Netherlands—has led to his fanbase being referred to as the _Orange Army_.[[385]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-389)[[386]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-390) Several races across Europe have dedicated Verstappen [grandstands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grandstand "Grandstand") to accommodate thousands of travelling Dutch fans, boosting ticket sales at Grands Prix such as in [Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgian_Grand_Prix "Belgian Grand Prix"), [Austria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Grand_Prix "Austrian Grand Prix") and [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Grand_Prix "Hungarian Grand Prix").[[387]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Smith_2018-391) A Verstappen grandstand featured at the inaugural [Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "Las Vegas Grand Prix") in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "2023 Las Vegas Grand Prix").[[388]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-392)
During the [2021 Dutch Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Dutch_Grand_Prix "2021 Dutch Grand Prix"), the managing director of [Honda in Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One"), [Masashi Yamamoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masashi_Yamamoto_\(motorsport\)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Masashi Yamamoto \(motorsport\) \(page does not exist\)") [[ja](https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E5%B1%B1%E6%9C%AC%E9%9B%85%E5%8F%B2%20\(%E3%83%A2%E3%83%BC%E3%82%BF%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B9%E3%83%9D%E3%83%BC%E3%83%84\) "ja:山本雅史 \(モータースポーツ\)")], praised Verstappen's support, stating that "in the six years I've been involved with Honda F1, I've never seen such a great turnout as at the Dutch Grand Prix. It was like being in a football stadium."[[389]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-gpblog.com_2022-393) In October 2021, Verstappen was voted the most popular Formula One driver in an official worldwide survey conducted by [Nielsen Media Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research") and [Motorsport Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorsport_Network "Motorsport Network"), earning 14.4% of the vote with particular success in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan").[[390]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Galloway_2021-394)[[391]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-395)
The fan-made song "[Super Max!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Max! "Super Max!")", performed by the [Pitstop Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitstop_Boys?action=edit&redlink=1 "Pitstop Boys \(page does not exist\)") [[nl](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pitstop%20Boys "nl:Pitstop Boys")] in 2016, went viral after his victory at the [2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"), topping the [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") _Viral 50_ chart in the Netherlands and reaching number two in the United Kingdom.[[392]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Gamble_2021-396) Another fan-made [EDM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music") track "33 Max Verstappen", was released in 2023, eventually going viral on social media due to [internet memes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_meme "Internet meme") referencing the hook: "tu tu tu du, Max Verstappen" (sometimes also written as "du du du du, Max Verstappen").[[393]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-397)[[394]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-398)
## Other racing
### Sportscar racing
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d3/MSR_GTP_WGI23_11.jpg/250px-MSR_GTP_WGI23_11.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:MSR_GTP_WGI23_11.jpg)The [Acura ARX-06](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acura_ARX-06 "Acura ARX-06") (pictured in 2023) tested by Verstappen with [Honda Racing Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_Racing_Corporation "Honda Racing Corporation") in November 2024.
Verstappen tested the [Honda NSX-GT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_NSX_\(second_generation\)#Super_GT "Honda NSX \(second generation\)")—a [GT500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_GT#GT500 "Super GT") class [Super GT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_GT "Super GT") car—during the 2022 [Honda Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_Racing_Corporation "Honda Racing Corporation") _Thanks Day_ event at [Motegi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobility_Resort_Motegi "Mobility Resort Motegi").[[395]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-399) After winning the event's [kart race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kart_racing "Kart racing") alongside [Marc Márquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_M%C3%A1rquez "Marc Márquez"), Honda awarded Verstappen—the first [Honda-powered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_in_Formula_One "Honda in Formula One") World Drivers' Champion since [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_Formula_One_World_Championship "1991 Formula One World Championship")—with an [NSX Type S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_NSX_\(second_generation\)#NSX_Type_S_\(2022\) "Honda NSX \(second generation\)").[[396]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-400) He later tested a Red Bull–liveried [Nissan Z NISMO GT500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nissan_Z_\(RZ34\)#Super_GT "Nissan Z \(RZ34\)") at [Fuji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuji_Speedway "Fuji Speedway") prior to the [2026 Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2026 Japanese Grand Prix").[[397]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-401)
In January 2024, Verstappen drove the [Ferrari 296 GT3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_296_GT3 "Ferrari 296 GT3") at the [Portimão](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algarve_International_Circuit "Algarve International Circuit"), as part of a two-day test with [Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutsche_Tourenwagen_Masters "Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters") team [Emil Frey Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Frey_Racing "Emil Frey Racing") alongside [Thierry Vermeulen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Vermeulen "Thierry Vermeulen"),[[398]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-402) who competed under the _Verstappen.com Racing_ banner in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Deutsche_Tourenwagen_Masters "2023 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters").[[399]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-403) Team principal Lorenz Frey-Hilti stated "there were also other [GT3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_GT3 "Group GT3") cars that day, but I can only say that Verstappen was driving on a different level than the rest. There are good drivers who cannot shine in a GT3 car due to a lack of experience, but Max is different. If something has four wheels, then [he's fast in it]", adding that he was "world-class".[[400]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-404)
On 19 November 2024, Verstappen drove a [prototype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_prototype "Sports prototype") for the first time, testing the [Acura ARX-06](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acura_ARX-06 "Acura ARX-06") with [Honda Racing Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_Racing_Corporation "Honda Racing Corporation") at [Las Vegas Motor Speedway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Motor_Speedway "Las Vegas Motor Speedway"), ahead of the [Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix").[[401]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-405) Verstappen expressed his desire to compete in the [24 Hours of Daytona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_Hours_of_Daytona "24 Hours of Daytona") and [Le Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_Hours_of_Le_Mans "24 Hours of Le Mans") after the test, stating that "it's just about finding the time".[[402]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-406)
In May 2025, he entered testing for the third round of the [2025 Nürburgring Langstrecken-Serie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_N%C3%BCrburgring_Langstrecken-Serie "2025 Nürburgring Langstrecken-Serie") in the 296 under the [pseudonym](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudonym "Pseudonym") "Franz Hermann", where he claimed to set an unofficial [GT3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Group_GT3 "Group GT3") lap record, reportedly in an attempt to obtain a licence to compete on the _[Nordschleife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nordschleife "Nordschleife")_.[[403]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-407)[[404]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-408) He received an [FIA Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Platinum "FIA Platinum") licence later that month, allowing him to compete in top-level [endurance racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endurance_racing_\(motorsport\) "Endurance racing \(motorsport\)").[[405]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-409)
In September 2025, he made his competitive debut on the _Nordschleife_ in the seventh round for [Lionspeed GP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionspeed_GP "Lionspeed GP"), completing the laps required for a GT3 permit in a [horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engine_power "Engine power")-restricted [Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 CS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche_718_Boxster_and_Cayman_\(982\)#718_Cayman_GT4_and_718_Spyder "Porsche 718 Boxster and Cayman \(982\)") as he finished seventh in-class.[[406]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-410) Later the same month, Verstappen made his GT3 race debut and won. He drove for [Emil Frey Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Frey_Racing "Emil Frey Racing"), racing a [Ferrari 296 GT3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari_296#Ferrari_296_GT3 "Ferrari 296") with [Chris Lulham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Lulham "Chris Lulham") in the [Nürburgring Endurance Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%BCrburgring_Langstrecken-Serie "Nürburgring Langstrecken-Serie").[[407]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-411) This start also made Max Verstappen the first defending Formula One World Champion to simultaneously compete in Formula One and another racing series since [Keke Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg"), who made a one-off appearance in the [1983 World Sportscar Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_World_Sportscar_Championship "1983 World Sportscar Championship"), also at the Nürburgring Nordschleife.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] After qualifying third, Verstappen, who drove the first stint, passed two cars and began to create a gap of over a minute. Verstappen handed the car to teammate Lulham for the second stint; Lulham crossed the line to win the race for the team, 24 seconds ahead of the car in second place.[[408]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-412)
In preparation for his participation at the [2026 24 Hours of Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_24_Hours_of_N%C3%BCrburgring "2026 24 Hours of Nürburgring"), Verstappen took part in the second round of the [2026 Nürburgring Langstrecken-Serie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_N%C3%BCrburgring_Langstrecken-Serie "2026 Nürburgring Langstrecken-Serie"), driving a [Mercedes-AMG GT3 Evo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-AMG_GT#AMG_GT3_Evo_\(2020%E2%80%93present\) "Mercedes-AMG GT") run by [Winward Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winward_Racing "Winward Racing").[[409]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-AMG2026-413) In a qualifying session affected by multiple [code 60 sections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_60_flag "Code 60 flag"), Verstappen put together a clean lap and achieved his maiden NLS pole position.[[410]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-414) After fighting for the lead with [Christopher Haase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Haase "Christopher Haase") throughout the opening stint, the No. 3 Verstappen Mercedes-AMG broke away from the field, allowing Verstappen, [Daniel Juncadella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Juncadella "Daniel Juncadella"), and [Jules Gounon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules_Gounon "Jules Gounon") to win by almost a minute.[[411]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-415)[[412]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-416) Following the race, the team was disqualified for using seven sets of tyres, which exceeded the limit of six allowed for race day.[[413]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-417)[[414]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-418)
### Sim racing
In his free time, Verstappen competes in [sim racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sim_racing "Sim racing"). Verstappen stated that it helps him with his real-life racing, keeping him "ready to go".[[415]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-RacingNews365-419) In 2015, he became a member of [Team Redline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Team_Redline "Team Redline"), a European professional sim racing team.[[416]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-420)[[417]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-421) On 23 March 2026, he absorbed the team into his wider Verstappen Racing motorsport project, rebranding the esports organization to [Verstappen Sim Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verstappen_Sim_Racing "Verstappen Sim Racing"). As part of the rebrand, the team now also serves as a driver development pathway from virtual racing into real-world competition.[[418]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-422)
He has also gained notoriety from critics for his sim racing activities clashing with Grand Prix weekends in some cases, most notably in the [2024 Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2024 Hungarian Grand Prix"), where he criticised [Red Bull Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing")'s strategy calls and the [RB20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing_RB20 "Red Bull Racing RB20")'s lack of performance over team radio. Verstappen had taken part in an _iRacing_ sim racing event prior to the Grand Prix, racing until 3:00 a.m.[[419]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-423)
#### iRacing special events (2020–present)
See also: [iRacing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IRacing "IRacing")
Verstappen has competed in several marquee events on _[iRacing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IRacing "IRacing")_ since February 2019, when he entered the _[Bathurst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Panorama "Mount Panorama") 12 Special Event_—a 12-hour virtual team [endurance race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endurance_racing_\(motorsport\) "Endurance racing \(motorsport\)")—alongside [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris").[[420]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-424) The pair won the _[Spa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spa-Francorchamps "Spa-Francorchamps") 24 Special Event_ in July.[[421]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-425) Verstappen won the _[Petit Le Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petit_Le_Mans "Petit Le Mans") Special Event_ in October 2020.[[422]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-426) Later that year, [Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_F1_Team "Haas F1 Team") driver and _R8G eSports_ founder [Romain Grosjean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romain_Grosjean "Romain Grosjean") deemed Verstappen to be the "fastest" driver in sim racing.[[423]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-427) He entered the eighth round of the 2023 _AMX Global League_ at [Imola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imola_Circuit "Imola Circuit"), winning the first heat.[[424]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-ATK-428)
Verstappen entered the _[Daytona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daytona_International_Speedway "Daytona International Speedway") 24 Special Event_ in January 2024, winning the [GTD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMSA_SportsCar_Championship#GT_Daytona_\(GTD\) "IMSA SportsCar Championship") class with Redline.[[425]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-429) In May, Verstappen received media attention for entering the _[Nürburgring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N%C3%BCrburgring "Nürburgring") 24 Special Event_ on the same weekend as the [Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "2024 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix");[[426]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-430) he won both events, achieving a [record-equalling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_consecutive_pole_positions "List of Formula One driver records") eighth consecutive pole position at the latter. Following his victory at the former, Ed Hardy of _[Autosport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autosport "Autosport")_ opined that Verstappen had "firmly established himself as one of the best sim racers in the world".[[424]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-ATK-428) Verstappen won his second _Spa 24 Special Event_ in July that year, completing a perfect season of 24-hour special events.[[427]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-431)
#### Le Mans Virtual (2020–2023)
See also: [24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_Hours_of_Le_Mans_Virtual "24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual"), [Le Mans Virtual Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Mans_Virtual_Series "Le Mans Virtual Series"), and [rFactor 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RFactor_2 "RFactor 2")
Verstappen competed in the [24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_Hours_of_Le_Mans_Virtual "24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual") on _[rFactor 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RFactor_2 "RFactor 2")_ in [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_24_Hours_of_Le_Mans_Virtual "2020 24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual"), [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_24_Hours_of_Le_Mans_Virtual "2022 24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual") and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_24_Hours_of_Le_Mans_Virtual?action=edit&redlink=1 "2023 24 Hours of Le Mans Virtual \(page does not exist\)")—hosted by [Automobile Club de l'Ouest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automobile_Club_de_l'Ouest "Automobile Club de l'Ouest") and the [FIA World Endurance Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_World_Endurance_Championship "FIA World Endurance Championship")—as well as two further rounds of the [2022–23 Le Mans Virtual Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Le_Mans_Virtual_Series "2022–23 Le Mans Virtual Series") in the [LMP2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LMP2 "LMP2") class.[[424]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-ATK-428) He described the former competition as a "clown show" after a technical issue saw him retire from the lead of the 2023 edition,[[428]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-432) subsequently finishing runner-up in the overall championship to [Porsche Coanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porsche_in_motorsport "Porsche in motorsport").[[424]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-ATK-428)

[rallying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rallying "Rallying") and [Thierry Vermeulen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Vermeulen "Thierry Vermeulen") in the [ADAC GT Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADAC_GT_Masters "ADAC GT Challenge Europe Sprint Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_GT_World_Challenge_Europe_Sprint_Cup "2023 GT World Challenge Europe Sprint Cup") and the [Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Deutsche_Tourenwagen_Masters "2023 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters"), linking up with [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferrari "Ferrari") customer [Emil Frey Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emil_Frey_Racing "Emil Frey Racing").[[431]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-435) In 2025, in conjunction with this effort, of Spa").[[433]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-437)

## Personal life
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/PH-DTF_Dassault_Falcon_900EX_%28Exxaero%29.jpg/250px-PH-DTF_Dassault_Falcon_900EX_%28Exxaero%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PH-DTF_Dassault_Falcon_900EX_\(Exxaero\).jpg)Verstappen's former aircraft (PH-DTF) at [Luton Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luton_Airport "Luton Airport") in 2022
Verstappen holds [dual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_citizenship "Dual citizenship") Dutch and Belgian citizenship, and decided to compete with a Dutch racing licence, as his father [Jos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos_Verstappen "Jos Verstappen") did. He stated in 2014 that he "feels more Dutch", having spent more time with his father than with his mother during his childhood, as well as his upbringing in [Maaseik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maaseik "Maaseik"), a Belgian town at the Dutch border.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-nationality2-9) The following year, Verstappen added that he "actually only lived in Belgium to sleep", and that he "was raised as a Dutch person and that's how [he feels]".[[437]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-441) In 2022, Verstappen stated that he appreciates both sides and is "half-half at the end of the day".[[438]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-442) In addition to his [native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_language "Dutch language") Dutch, he is fluent in English and [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"), with limited proficiency in [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language").[[439]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-443)
He competed in Formula One for over a season before obtaining a road driving licence on his 18th birthday.[[440]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-444) Verstappen moved to [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") in October 2015 where he has lived ever since.[[441]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-GPNov15-445) In November 2020, Verstappen bought a [Dassault Falcon 900EX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Falcon_900 "Dassault Falcon 900") aircraft from [Virgin Galactic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgin_Galactic "Virgin Galactic"). The aircraft, [registered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_registration "Aircraft registration") PH-DTF, was operated by Exxaero.[[442]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Falcon-446) In January 2025, he acquired a Mangusta GranSport 33 yacht, named _Unleash the Lion_.[[443]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Yacht-447) The following month, he sold the Falcon 900EX and purchased a [Dassault Falcon 8X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dassault_Falcon_8X "Dassault Falcon 8X"), registered PH-UTL, which is also operated by Exxaero.[[444]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-Falcon8x-448)
Verstappen is a supporter of the [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") and [PSV Eindhoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSV_Eindhoven "PSV Eindhoven") football clubs.[[445]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-449) In September 2022, he was appointed an Officer of the [Order of Orange-Nassau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Orange-Nassau "Order of Orange-Nassau") in recognition of his racing achievements.[[446]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-auto-450) Verstappen has been dating Brazilian-Dutch model [Kelly Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Piquet "Kelly Piquet"), daughter of three-time World Drivers' Champion [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet"), since October 2020.[[447]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-451)[[448]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-452) They had their first daughter in April 2025.[[449]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-453)

#### Formula One records
Main article: [List of career achievements by Max Verstappen § Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_career_achievements_by_Max_Verstappen#Records "List of career achievements by Max Verstappen")
Verstappen made his Formula One debut at the [2015 Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Australian_Grand_Prix "2015 Australian Grand Prix"), and has since gone on to hold [over 90 records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_career_achievements_by_Max_Verstappen#Records "List of career achievements by Max Verstappen") in Formula One, including [most wins in a season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_wins_in_a_season "List of Formula One driver records") (19), [most podium finishes in a season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_podium_finishes_in_a_season "List of Formula One driver records") (21), [most consecutive wins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_consecutive_wins "List of Formula One driver records") (10), and [most consecutive pole positions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_driver_records#Most_consecutive_pole_positions "List of Formula One driver records") (8).

Is he badly hurt in there?'";[[370]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-373) Verstappen later revealed that he raced with severe blurred vision after the crash. He described seeing "wavy" or "blurry" images, particularly on bumpy circuits like [COTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_of_the_Americas "Circuit of the Americas") at the [2021 United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_United_States_Grand_Prix "2021 United States Grand Prix"), where he almost stopped.[[371]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-374)[[372]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen#cite_note-375) The other notable incident occurred at the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Italian_Grand_Prix "2021 Italian Grand Prix"), where Verstappen's car was stacked on top of Hamilton's after a kerb sent him upward.
